Registered name: Paula Amanda Miles.
Age on the registration profile: 40.

Pre-clerking Doctor
Dr. David Wilfred Morley (FY1)

Presenting Complaint
Chronic left hip pain due to end-stage OA.

Procedure
Totalleft hip replacement

History of Presenting Complaint
Site: L hip. Onset: Gradual onset over the past 5 yrs, worsening in the last 12 mths. Character: Constant, dull ache with sharp exacerbations during movement. Radiates: Occasionally radiates to the L knee. Associations: Increased stiffness, reduced ROM, difficulty walking. Timing: Pain is worse in the evening and after prolonged activity. Exa cerbating factors: Weight-bearing and prolonged standing. Severity: 8/10 at its worst, 4/10 at rest.

Past Medical History
- HTN
- Mild asthma

Medications
- Paracetamol 500mg as needed
- Ibuprofen 400mg twice daily

Allergies
NKDA

Social History
- Lives alone in a bungalow, independent with ADLs. - Mobilises with a walking stick indoors. Requires a W/C for plonger distances outdoors. - Ex-smoker, quit 5 years ago. Smoked 10 PY. - Drinks alcohol occasionally (approx. 5-6 units/week). - No recreational drug use.

Family History
No significant family history of OA or other musculoskeletal conditions. No family history of CVD r sudden cardiac death.

On Examination
Alert, comfortable at rest. Mobilises with walking stick. A: Patent airway, no stridor or wheeze. B: Vesicular breath sounds bilaterally. No wheeze or crackles. C: Heart sounds dual. No murmurs or added sounds. Peripheral phlses palpable. No oedema. D: Power 4/5 in lower limbs bilaterally. Left hip movement restricted with pain on flexion and internal rotation.  No focal neuro deficit. E: No skin lesions or erythema over left hip. Skin intact.

Observations
HR 78 bpm
BP 142/88 mmHg
RR 16 br/min
Temp 36.8Â°C
SpO2 98%

Investigations
ECG: Borderline prolonged QT interval (QTc: 470ms). Referred to anaesthetics team for review. FBC, U&E, and coag prrofile performed. All results pending.

Plan
- Referral to anaesthetics team to review borderline prolonged QTc interval (QTc: 470ms).
- Advise patient to bring inhaler on the day of surgery.
- No new meds prescribed.
- Optimise asthma control and ensure inhaler technique is satisfactory.
- Proced with planned surgery on 06/01/26, as scheduled.

Presenting Complaint
Progressive deformity of the left leg.

Procedure
Hemiepiphysiodesis of the left distal femur

History of Presenting Complaint
- Deformity of left leg noted over the past year by parents.
- Gradual worsening with increased prominence.
- No associated pain or swelling.
- No trauma or injury reported.
- No fucntional limitations noted; patient remains active and mobile.
- Referred by GP for ortho evaluation and surgical correction.

None reported.

Medications
None currently prescribed.

Allergies
No known drug or food allergies.

Social History
- Lives with parents and sibling in a non-smoking household.
- Attends primary school, no concerns regarding school attendance or performance.
- Active, participates in age-appropriate physical activities.
- No EtOH, smoking, or recreational drug use.

Family History
- No family history of MSK deformities or related conditions.
- No family history of bleeding disorders or other significant medical conditions.

On Examination
- Alert, interactive, and well-appearing 8-year-old girl.  
- Mild pallor noted, likely related to borderline Hb levels (10.2 g/dL).

- Patient cleared for surgery pending satisfactory Hb level after repeat test.

- Hyperlipidaemia
- Osteoporosis

Penicillin

- Lives alone in a ground-flor flat

- Drinks alcohol rarely (1-2 units per month)
- No regular exercise due to pain
- Retired school teacher

- Mother: Osteoporosis
- Father: HTN

documents.text:
Registered name: Margaret Sarah Holland.
Age on the registration profile: 56.

Pre-clerking Doctor
Dr. Min Song (FY1)

Presenting Complaint
Zevere right hip pain due to OA.

Procedure
Total right ihp replacement for end stage OA

History of Presenting Complaint
Site: Right hip. Onset: Gradual worsening over the past 8 years. Character: Constant, dull ache with intermittent sharp exacerbations. Radiates: Down the right thigh to the knee. Associations: Stiffnss and reduced mobility. Timing: Present daily, worse in the evening. Exaecrbating factors: Standing, walking, and climbing stairs. Severity: 7-8/10 on most days.

Past Medical History
- Osteoarthritis diagnosed 8 years ago
- HTN diagnosed 5 years ago

Medications
- Ramipril 2.5 mg OD (newly prescribed)
- No other current meds.

Allergies
No known allergies.

Social History
- Lives in a single-storey house with spouse.
- Mobilises with a walking stifk.
- Requires assistance with dressing and bathing.
- Non-smoker.
- Drinks 5 units of alochol per week.
- Retired office worker.

Family History
Father had HTN. No family history of osteoarthritis or oter significant conditions reported.

On Examination
Patjent appears well and not in acute distress. Cardiovascular: Normal heart sounds with no murmurs or added sounds. Peripheral pulses present and equal bilaterally. Respiratory: Chest clear to auscultation. No wheeze or crackles. Abdominal: Soft and non-tender. No organomegaly. Musculoskeleatl: Severe tenderness over the right hip. Reduced ROM on flexion, abduction, and internal rotation. Antalgic gait observed. Left hip and other joints unremarkable. Neurological: Normal sensation and motor function in both lower limbs. Reflexes present and symmetrical.

Observations
HR 78
BP 146/90
RR 16
Temp 36.7
SpO2 98%

Investigations
ECG: Normal sinus rhythm, no significant abnormalities. FBC: Normal. Renal function: Normal.

Plan
- Start ramipril 2.5 mg OD to optimize BP.
- Schedule a follow-up BP check with GP in 5 days to assess response tto treatment.
- Proceed with planned surgery on 06/01/26 if BP well-controlled.
- Provide pre-operative fasting instructions closer to the admission dtae.

Registered name: Brian William Morris.
Age on the registration profile: 76.

Pre-clerking Doctor
Dr. Idris Dad (SpR)

Presenting Complaint
Right shoulder pain and restricted movement.

Procedure
Total right shoulder replacement for end-stage OA.

History of Presenting Complaint
Site: Right shoulder. Onset: Gradual over several years. Character: Dull, constant ache with intermittent sharp exacerbations. Radiates: No radiation. Associations: Limited ROM, stiffness, difficulty sleeping due to pain. Timing: Pain is constant but worsens with activity. Exacerbating factors: Overhead movements, lifting objects. Severity: 8/10 at worst, 4/10 at rest.

Past Medical History
- HTN
- Hypercholesterolaemia
- OA
- Cataract surgery 2018

Medications
- Paracetamol 1 g QDS
- Ibuprofen 400 mg TDS with food
- Omeprazole 20 mg OD

Allergies
- Nuts

Social History
- Retired teacher. Lives with spouse in a bungalow. - Independent with ADLs but avoids strenuous tasks due to pain. - Non-smoker. Drinks 4 units of alcohol per week. - No recreational drug use. - Walks short distances daily with intermittent breaks due to joint discomfort.

Family History
- Father: Osteoarthritis (deceased at 82 from MI).
- Mother: HTN (deceased at 85 from stroke).

On Examination
- General: Alert, cooperative, no distress. BMI 27.5.
A: Patent airway, no stridor or wheeze.
B: Equal chest expansion, no added sounds.
C: Heart sounds dual, no murmurs. Peripheral pulses palpable.
D: Intact sensation and motor function in RUL. No focal neurological deficit.
E: Right shoulder: Deformity noted, with tenderness on palpation. Severe restriction in abd and ext rot. Crepitus on movement.

Observations
HR 76
BP 138/84
RR 16
Temp 36.8
SpO2 97%

Investigations
ECG: Minor age-related changes, no acute abnormalities.

Test Results
- FBC: Mild anaemia (Hb 11.2 g/dL), likely secondary to chronic disease.
- U&E: Normal.
- Coag profile: Normal.

Plan
1. Start ferrous sulfate 200 mg BD to optimise Hb prior to surgery. 2. Continue current antihypertensive and lipid-lowering therapy. 3. Advise dietary modifications to address anaemia (increase iron-rich foods). 4. Proceed with planned surgery on 05/01/26 as no contraindications identified. 5. Ensure pre-operative blood tests are repeated on admision day to confirm optimised Hb levels.


Dr. Idris Dad (Specialty Registrar)

Registered name: Hope Chinwo.
Age on the registration profile: 75.

Pre-clerking Doctor
Dr. Brian Anthony Payne (FY1)

Presenting Complaint
Severe left hip pain due to end-stage OA.

Procedure
Total left hip replacement

History of Presenting Complaint
Site: Left hip Onset: Gradual, worsening over past 5 yrs Character: Deep, aching painRadiates: None Associations: Limited mobility, stiffnes, mild fatigue Timing: Constant, worse w/ prolonged standing/walking Exacerbating factors: Weight-bearing, activity Severity: 8/10

Past Medical History
- HTN
- OA (severe, left hip)
- Cataract surgery (2018)

Medications
- Paracetamol 500mg PRN
- Calcium w/ Vit D supplements

Allergies
None

Social History
- Lives alone in ground-floor flat
- Mobilises w/ stick indoors, frame outdoors
- Independent in ADLs but slow
- Non-smoker, noalcohol, no recreational drugs
- Retired teacher

Family History
Mother: HTN Father: T2DM

On Examination
Looks well, no distress. CVS: HS I + II + 0, no murmurs. Resp: Chest clear, good air entry bilat. No wheeze/crackkles. Abdo: Soft, non-tender, no masses. L hip: Pain on palpation and ROM. Severe restriction in flexion and int rot. No redness/swelling. LL: Pulses palpable bilat. No oedema. No signs of DVT. Neuro LLs: Power 4/5 L hip flex/ext due to pain. Sensation intact bilat.

Observations
HR 78
BP 145/85
RR 16
Temp 36.9
SpO2 97%

Investigations
ECG: NSR, no ischaemic changes

Test Results
Hb: 11.3 g/dL (mild anaemia) WCC, platelets, renal fx: Normal LFTs: Normal

Plan
- Start ferrous sulfate 200 mg OD for anaemia
- Contact GP for BP monitoring andoptimisation
- Proceed w/ elective total L hip replacement as planned
- Pre-op anaesthetic review on admission day
